anomalies.description: A sudden large plume of white smoke erupts from the rear/midsection of a moving bus at approximately 27.0s, rapidly expanding and obscuring the vehicle and surrounding area over the next few seconds. The onset is abrupt with no visible preceding collision or mechanical failure (e.g., no impact with another vehicle), consistent with an explosion or sudden catastrophic failure (e.g., fuel tank rupture or device detonation). Traffic continues momentarily but vehicles begin to swerve and slow as the smoke spreads, indicating an unexpected hazardous event.

A sudden large plume of white smoke/dust erupts in the middle of the road around frame 3 (32.5s), expanding rapidly across lanes without an obvious vehicle collision or fire source visible. The smoke appears instantaneously and grows outward in a manner consistent with an explosion or sudden burst (e.g., gas cylinder rupture or IED). Traffic continues but some rickshaws and pedestrians appear to react by slowing or veering away. No clear flash is visible due to camera exposure, but the abrupt onset and volume of smoke strongly suggest an explosive incident.
